clue.text: New gear after work, girls? Aida may look better with these on

definitions.text: Aida may look better with these on

indicators.note: the reworked gear comes after the word for work in the answer

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: new gear is gear made over, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Someone fits out a work with new kit and girls, then wonders whether the opera Aida looks better through lenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on 'gear', not an adjective. Aida is a Verdi opera, so the definition hints at what a theatregoer might hold up to view it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small binoculars used in a theatre help an audience member see an opera such as Aida more clearly.

clue.text: Petty officer upset with media abuse

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for a petty officer in the navy
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: A naval officer is annoyed by how the newspapers mistreat people.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to treat cruelly and unjustly, a form of mistreatment or ill use.

clue.text: Pretend to follow former lover's demand

indicators.note: the word for pretend comes after the former lover in the answer

parts.note: an ex is a former partner; the 's stands for has, joining the pieces
to act is to pretend

explanation.surface: An ex-partner insists on joining in the pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to insist on or require something, such as payment or obedience, as a verb.

clue.text: PM almost nobody supports later

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: after means later, as in 'soon after'

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: no one means nobody

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister finds almost no one backs him later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister but stands for post meridiem. 'Almost' cuts NO ONE to NOON, which sits under AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, from Latin post meridiem, marks the hours after midday, the period of the day called afternoon.

clue.text: Avoid John's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, a loo, so john's gives loos

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to steer clear of John's radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name but is slang for a toilet; LOO is British for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose a pursuer is to evade or shake them off, so the verbs share that sense of escaping.

clue.text: South American writers beginning to experience apprehension

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
US stands for American, as in US citizen
pens are writing implements

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: South American authors start to feel anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty felt while waiting to learn what happens, a state of nervous expectation.

clue.text: In regret, neighbour turned up record

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in means the letters lie inside the clue's words regret neighbour

explanation.surface: Regretfully, the neighbour came along with a gramophone disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' finds RETNE spanning 'regret, neighbour'; 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record them, for example writing data into a ledger or log.

clue.text: Bear in mind politician is under fire? Not half!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the politician sits under the trimmed word, so it comes second
not half means only the second half of the word fire is kept, the first half being dropped

parts.note: a Member of Parliament is a politician

explanation.surface: Is a politician under attack? Very much so, as the exclamation implies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much', but here it trims FIRE to RE, with MEMBER below.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember something is to keep it in your thoughts, an idiom for not forgetting.

clue.text: Plant that can sting bug

definitions.meaning: the stinging ... is a plant whose hairs irritate the skin
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A plant that can sting an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging weed gives its name to the verb for irritating someone, and both senses fit bothering or annoying.

clue.text: Carpet is fixed with small drills

indicators.note: fixed means altered or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A carpet is laid down using small power drills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' and 'drills' suggest DIY, but 'fixed' is the anagram signal and 'drills' means rehearses.
explanation.definitionFit: Drills, as a verb, means rehearses repeatedly, which is the same as practises in British spelling.

clue.text: Skirt hem easily hides thread

indicators.note: hides means the answer is concealed inside the words skirt hem easily

explanation.surface: A skirt's hem conceals the stitching thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thread' looks like sewing cotton but means a running idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the thread or central subject running through a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Anger after hospital department's full

indicators.note: the word for anger follows the department in the answer

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital; the 's stands for is
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Fury erupts after a hospital ward fills up.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, with nothing left out, the same as full in that sense.

clue.text: Most jolly times involved embracing sin

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece within it
involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters of times are mixed up

parts.note: to err is to do wrong, to sin

explanation.surface: The happiest occasions turned out to involve some wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' turns TIMES into MIEST, which embraces ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriest is the superlative of merry, meaning the most cheerful or jolly.

clue.text: Smells, on reflection, concealing a flavour

indicators.note: concealing means the word for smells, reversed, holds the next piece inside
on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: noses means smells, as in sniffs out

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs and, thinking it over, hides a taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reverses NOSES to SESON, and 'concealing' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To season food is to flavour it with salt, herbs or spices; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Organised golf with my boss south of Scottish island

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so these letters come after

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the setter's boss is the newspaper editor, ED

explanation.surface: A round of golf with the boss is fixed up on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN is an island off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged means set out or planned in order, the same as organised.

clue.text: Meet doctor she blames leaving hospital

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
leaving means the letter for hospital goes out of the word she

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient meets a doctor whom she blames, as she leaves hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but means rearrange; take H from SHE BLAMES and anagram the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet, in the sense of a group coming together, is to gather or assemble.

clue.text: Renovated castle, keeping area or moving staircase?

indicators.note: keeping means holding the next piece inside
renovated means done up, so the letters of castle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restored castle, with its grounds, might get a moving staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renovated' rearranges the castle letters into ESCALT, and 'keeping' puts the area letter inside before the final two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a powered staircase whose steps move continuously, as in shops and stations.

clue.text: Exciting Republican in charge after vote

indicators.note: the Republican and in charge pieces come after the vote

parts.note: to elect is to choose by voting

explanation.surface: A Republican is in charge after a thrilling election.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric, used figuratively, means thrilling or charged with excitement, as in an electric atmosphere.

clue.text: Is it wrong and sly to remove all leaders vigorously?

indicators.note: leaders are first letters, so every first letter of the words is is dropped from is, it, wrong and sly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is wrong and sneaky to oust every leader with force.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letters of 'Is it wrong ... sly' leaves S, T, RONG, LY; 'and' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongly and vigorously both describe acting with force and energy.

clue.text: Remarkably, Conservative initially isn't attending latest party

parts.note: so means remarkably, as in so good

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Strangely, a Tory is not at the newest political party at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' covers all four words, giving C, I, A, L after SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering, a noun sense.

clue.text: Son was concerned, getting frightened

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
cared means was concerned

explanation.surface: A son was worried and became afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and frightened both mean afraid; synonyms.

clue.text: Urged to change top getting dolled up

indicators.note: to change top means swapping out the first letter of the word for urged

parts.note: pressed means urged, as in pressed someone to act

explanation.surface: Someone was pushed into changing their shirt to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment but means the first letter: P changes to D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed in fine clothes is a synonym for dolled up, smartened for an occasion.

clue.text: Get reduced settlement

explanation.surface: Accept a smaller payout.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means shrink and the noun means a formal agreement, two separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Relationship from a little time in Brazilian city

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the city

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a city in Brazil
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A romance springs up after a short spell in Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relationship between two amounts.

clue.text: Delight from learner after parking with no trouble

indicators.note: the learner comes after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
L is for a learner driver, from the L-plate
ease means freedom from difficulty, no trouble

explanation.surface: A learner driver is thrilled to have parked without trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them pleasure, to delight them; both are verbs.

clue.text: In the centre, teenagers fight roughly

indicators.note: in the centre means only the middle letter of teenagers is taken

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight

explanation.surface: Teenagers brawl in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, the adverb sense of roughly.

clue.text: Variety of bread, however one looks at it

indicators.note: however one looks at it means the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: a flatbread from South Asian cooking

explanation.surface: A type of bread looks the same from any angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread of South Asian cooking, an example of a bread.

clue.text: Spy regularly wants to gather information

indicators.note: to gather means to hold the next piece within
regularly means every other letter of wants is taken

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy routinely seeks to collect intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes AT from wants, which gathers GEN, British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is an operative of a secret service, a spy.

clue.text: Responses concerning suits

parts.note: re means concerning, about
lawsuits are legal actions

explanation.surface: Replies about lawsuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suits' suggests clothing but means legal cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are replies or responses to something said or done.

clue.text: Focused on coin in case next to diamonds

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the case

parts.note: a crate is a packing case
a cent is a coin
D is the abbreviation for the card suit of diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone stares hard at a coin in its case beside some diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a display box for the coin but is a packing crate; 'next to' simply adds the diamonds letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated means with attention fixed intently on one thing, which is being focused.
